office.label: Downtown Atlanta
office.shortDescription: Downtown Atlanta concentrates office towers, government, convention activity and major institutions around the city’s historic center. Its high-rise business setting differs from Midtown’s Peachtree corridor and Buckhead’s northern office-and-retail concentration; individual blocks also shift between daytime business activity, hospitality and event uses.

office.label: Midtown Atlanta
office.oneLineDistinction: Office, arts and institutions along Peachtree
office.shortDescription: Midtown Atlanta follows Peachtree Street through a dense mix of offices, arts institutions, hotels and street-level restaurants. The corridor’s cultural anchors and continuous urban blocks distinguish it from Downtown’s civic core and Buckhead’s more dispersed commercial nodes.

retail.label: Buckhead
retail.oneLineDistinction: Regional offices and destination retail in north Atlanta
retail.shortDescription: Buckhead pairs major office buildings with destination shopping, hotels, restaurants and professional services in north Atlanta. Its regional retail role and multiple commercial nodes make it different from Midtown’s continuous Peachtree corridor and Downtown’s civic and convention center.

retail.label: Old Fourth Ward
retail.oneLineDistinction: Storefronts and dining around the BeltLine edge
retail.shortDescription: Old Fourth Ward combines neighborhood storefronts, restaurants and service businesses with former industrial buildings near the BeltLine’s Eastside Trail. Its smaller spaces and street-level activity create a more neighborhood-oriented retail setting than Buckhead’s regional centers.
whatStandsOut: Storefronts and dining around the BeltLine edge

industrial.label: Upper Westside / Bankhead
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Adaptive industrial buildings on Atlanta’s northwest side
industrial.shortDescription: Upper Westside and Bankhead retain warehouses, workshops and adapted industrial buildings along Atlanta’s northwest rail and road corridors. The area’s mix of active operating space and redevelopment differs from the more conventional southside industrial geography.

industrial.label: Southside / Lakewood
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Industrial and service land south of the core
industrial.shortDescription: Southside and Lakewood contain warehouse, service-industrial and production land south of Atlanta’s urban core. The district’s airport-adjacent market language requires care: only City-of-Atlanta locations belong here, while Hapeville, East Point and College Park remain separate.
